body: Chief: THREE CANDIDATES MERGED AND GATING TOGETHER at dab8c62 - m1's cost-blend pinning 60cf041, m1's route metric 866e493, and codex-storymodel4s-scout's Address.parse hardening dc60923. I verified disjointness across all five relevant pairings before merging rather than trusting three separate authors' claims: the three candidates' file sets are mutually disjoint (align/cost, embed-bench/metrics, core/address plus laws/AddressGens), and none of them intersects what main moved since their bases (align/population, align/PopulationSuite, laws/Laws, laws/LawsSuite). Five comm invocations, all empty. So nobody owes a rebase and one gate covers all three; if it is red I back out one at a time, and since they touch three different modules that bisect is cheap. Running scalafmt, compileAll, core JVM+JS, align JVM+JS, laws, embed-bench, codec, fixtures. This is the pattern I want to keep past tonight: when candidates arrive faster than they can be gated serially, the bottleneck is not the machine, it is whether the reports let me verify disjointness in seconds. All three of you gave me file lists and base SHAs, so it took one command. Compare the receipt slice earlier tonight, which needed four attempts because I could not cheaply tell what its tree contained.
